title.narrative: Modernization of Algeria Pub Proc Syst.

description.narrative: The proposed grant (US$400,000) would support Algeria priority activities under the Maghreb initiative as determined by the Algerian authorities. Grant funded activities would be implemented over a two-year period through the following two components: 1. Feasibility study and road map for the establishment of a national public procurement management system; 2. Design and implementation of a sustainable National Training and Capacity Building program in the area of Procurement. Component 1: Feasibility study and road map for the establishment of a national public procurement management system. (Estimated Grant Funding: US$ 220,000) The Grant would finance TA to (1) conduct a comprehensive analysis of the existing business processes, Information Systems, local capacity, and relevant regulatory environments; This analysis would covers both a System analysis, and a Business impact analysis (2) draw the road map for the establishment of the Public procurement management system, including cost estimate for implementation, customization and maintenance. The total cost of the feasibility study and road map is estimated at $220,000. Component 2: Design and implementation of a sustainable National Training and Capacity Building program in the area of Public Procurement. (Estimated Grant Funding: US$ 180,000) In support for the above program, the grant would fund activities needed for the initiation of a locally-based capacity building program including the selection of an International Training institute specialized in Public Procurement to: (a) conduct a needs assessment based on an initial review of available expertise; (b) design specific training modules for a training of Algerian trainers program; (c) implementation of the training of trainers' program; (d) assist local training institutes in the design and implementation of in-house permanent curriculum design and skills updates program for Public procurement practitioners; and (e) training of a first batch of Public procurement practitioners. The total cost of the above activity would be approximately US$ 180,000. This would be financed in full by the IDF
